chapter: Tom Brown's band and the first Dixieland claim
title: Marshall Stearns's 1937 letter to La Rocca
summary: The interviewer reads Stearns's January 1937 letter about the argument over colored musicians. La Rocca accuses Stearns of being pro-communist and says articles copied from him hurt a working man.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: The letter here from... Let me see. I'll give you the full letterhead. It's a letter from Marshall W. Stearns. Yale Hot Club, 6th Linwood Place, New Haven, Connecticut. M. W. Stearns, President. Charter Unit of the UHCA. January the 11th, 1937, Mr. D.J. La Rocca, Earl Theater, Washington, D.C. Dear Nick, I have all your records from Liberty Stable Blues to the recent disc. I like the earlier ones better. Between you and me, our last argument should furnish you with plenty of publicity. I do think, however, that you fail to give colored musicians a break. And that is why I exaggerated the other extreme, since the public is inclined to believe you and musicians of your opinion. There is nothing I should like better than to see your scrapbook. However, I am still in school and will be teaching next year. If I ever get the chance, I shall certainly drop in and say hello. Let's keep up the battle. Sincerely, Marshal W. Stearns. That's a signature, and it has M. W. Stearns, President, typed underneath. Its initials are given M. W. Stearns, and M. J. L. as his titus.

From this article, many other articles was copied. This is a work, you've got to be either pro-communist or a communist to work this way. There's a letter to keep me quiet. I'm a working man, trying to support a family. This man has not stopped writing about Negroes, yet he knows different. Now here's Brown's letter. To show you Brown was lying, I want to show you, I want to have him read this in there, what the name of his band was, in case you ever read Downbeat on 1936, and see what they have did to a man who has did nothing to anyone but tried to make a living and be honest in his ways of life. Would you read this letter here?
